docs.text:
The labels of the codes in the NIBRS master files.

Each codebook maps the codes of a field (as they are written in the master files) to their labels. The labels follow the reference tables that the FBI's Crime Data Explorer publishes with its NIBRS downloads (such as "NIBRS_OFFENSE_TYPE.csv"), and, for the fields that are only in the master files (such as the batch header's population group), the FBI's "NIBRS Flatfile Yearly Master Record Descriptions".

Codes changed over the years, and each codebook has every code that any year uses. A few codes meant something else in earlier years:

  • Race "A" was "Asian or Pacific Islander" before 2013, when "P" (Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander) was added.
  • Exceptional clearance "C" was "Extradition Denied" in the 1995 document and is "In Custody of Other Jurisdiction" now.
Contents

Codebooks

every codebook, by the name that crimepy.nibrs.layouts.Field uses. ACTIVITIES: the labels of criminal activities and gang information ("activities"). AGENCY_TYPES: the labels of agency types ("agency_types"). AGES: the labels of age codes of victims, offenders, and arrestees ("ages"). ARREST_TYPES: the labels of types of arrest ("arrest_types"). BIASES: the labels of bias motivations ("biases"). CIRCUMSTANCES: the labels of aggravated assault and homicide circumstances ("circumstances"). COMPLETIONS: whether an offense was attempted or completed ("completions"). DISPOSITIONS: the labels of dispositions of arrestees under 18 ("dispositions"). DRUGS: the labels of types of suspected drugs ("drugs"). ENTRIES: whether force was used to enter ("entries"). ETHNICITIES: the labels of ethnicities ("ethnicities"). EXCEPTIONAL_CLEARANCES: the labels of exceptional clearances ("clearances"). INJURIES: the labels of types of injury ("injuries"). JUSTIFICATIONS: the labels of justifiable homicide circumstances ("justifications"). LOCATIONS: the labels of types of location ("locations"). LOSSES: the labels of types of property loss ("losses"). MEASURES: the labels of units of drug quantities ("measures"). MULTIPLE_ARRESTEES: the labels of multiple arrestee indicators ("multiple_arrestees"). OFFICER_ACTIVITIES: the labels of what officers who were killed or assaulted were doing ("officer_activities"). OFFICER_ASSIGNMENTS: the labels of assignments of officers who were killed or assaulted ("officer_assignments"). POPULATION_GROUPS: the labels of agencies' population groups ("population_groups"). PROPERTIES: the labels of property descriptions ("properties"). RACES: the labels of races ("races"). REGIONS: the labels of the Census regions of agencies ("regions"). RELATIONSHIPS: the labels of victims' relationships to offenders ("relationships"). RESIDENTS: whether a victim or arrestee is a resident ("residents"). SEXES: the labels of sexes ("sexes"). SUBREGIONS: the labels of the Census divisions of agencies ("divisions"). USING: what offenders were suspected of using ("using"). VICTIM_TYPES: the labels of types of victim ("victim_types"). WEAPONS: the labels of types of weapon or force ("weapons"). OFFENSES: the name, category, whom or what it is against, and group of each offense code. The names are the "offenses" codebook. OFFENSE_CATEGORIES: the category of each offense code (such as "Assault Offenses"). CRIMES_AGAINST: whom or what each offense is against ("Person", "Property", "Society", or "Not a Crime"). OFFENSE_GROUPS: whether each offense is in Group "A" or Group "B". OFFENSE_TYPES: the offense codes of each type: whom or what they are against (as in CRIMES_AGAINST), and "National Security Offenses", "Rape Offenses", "Sex Offenses", and "Immigration Offenses". STATE_ABBREVIATIONS: the postal abbreviation of each numeric state code. STATES: the name of each numeric state code (the "states" codebook). AGE_YEARS: the age in years of each special age code.

docs.title: layouts
docs.text:
Where each field is in the records of the NIBRS master files.

A NIBRS master file has one record (line) for each segment of each report. The first two characters of a record name its segment (its "level"), and the rest are fixed-width fields. The positions are those of the FBI's "NIBRS Flatfile Yearly Master Record Descriptions" (12/18/95), which is still the documentation that the Crime Data Explorer gives with the files, and of the fields that the FBI added later and that are in the files but not in that document:

  • Administrative segment (01), position 89: cargo theft (Y or N), in 2013 and later.
  • Offense segment (02), positions 60-67: bias motivations #2 to #5, in 2013 to 2016.
  • Victim segment (04), positions 124-135: the officer's activity and assignment, and the ORI of another jurisdiction (handwritten in the document), in every year.
  • Offender segment (05), position 40: the ethnicity of the offender, in 2013 and later.
  • Batch header (BH), positions 285-292: a date that is the same for every agency in a state, in 2013 to 2016.

Files before 2013 split each agency's batch header into three records ("B1", "B2", and "B3"), and files from 2013 on have one ("BH"). Their fields have the same names here, so crimepy makes one table of agencies from either.

Positions in Field are those of Python slices (counted from 0, with the end excluded), so the document's positions "34-36" are start = 33, end = 36. Records shorter than a layout (most records after 2012 drop trailing blanks) are padded with blanks, so fields past their end are missing.

Contents

Field: a field of a record: its name, position, and kind. Layout: the fields of one kind of record. KINDS: the kinds of fields. LAYOUTS: the layout of each segment level, by its two-character code. TABLES: the name of the table made from each segment level. SEGMENTS: the segment levels of each table.

docs.title: munge
docs.text:
Makes tables of NIBRS data ready for analysis in pandas.

prepare is applied to every table that crimepy.nibrs.read and crimepy.nibrs.load return. It keeps every column and adds:

  • Every table: state, the postal abbreviation of the state.
  • Victims, offenders, and arrestees: victim_age, offender_age, and arrestee_age, the age in years (0 for a baby under a year old, 99 for 99 or older, and missing if unknown). The age codes are kept as victim_age_code, and so on.
  • Offenses, arrestees, and Group "B" arrests: offense_category, crime_against, and offense_group of the offense (with the prefix "arrest_" for arrests).
  • Agencies: population, the population of all of the agency's counties, and months_active, the number of months in which the agency submitted a report (of incidents or of no incidents).

With decode = True (the default), codes are replaced with their labels (such as "Residence/Home" for location "20"), as categories. Codes that are not in a codebook are kept as they are. decode turns the codes of a table loaded with decode = False into labels later.

Contents

CODE_COLUMNS: the codebook of each column of codes. add_ages: adds the age in years of each age code. add_offense_details: adds the category, target, and group of offenses. decode: replaces codes with their labels. prepare: makes a table ready for analysis. to_pandas: makes a pyarrow table into a pandas data frame.

def add_ages(data: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Adds the age in years of each column of age codes.

    A column "victim_age_code" gets a column "victim_age" after it, and so
    on. Babies under a year old ("NN", "NB", and "BB") are 0, "99" (99 or
    older) is 99, and an unknown age ("00") is missing.

    Args:
        data: a table with columns of age codes, whose names end in
            "_age_code".

    Returns:
        The table, with the ages.

    """
    for column in [c for c in data.columns if str(c).endswith('_age_code')]:
        name = str(column).removesuffix('_code')
        if name in data.columns:
            continue
        values = _lookup(data[column], _age_years)
        data.insert(
            _after(data, column), name, pd.to_numeric(values).astype('Int64'))
    return data

def add_offense_details(data: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Adds the category, target, and group of each offense.

    "offense_code" gets "offense_category", "crime_against", and
    "offense_group" after it, and "arrest_offense" gets the same columns with
    the prefix "arrest_". Only codes are looked up, so this is done before
    the codes are decoded.

    Args:
        data: a table with an "offense_code" or "arrest_offense" column of
            codes.

    Returns:
        The table, with the details.

    """
    for column, prefix in (('offense_code', ''), ('arrest_offense', 'arrest_')):
        if (column not in data.columns
                or f'{prefix}offense_category' in data.columns):
            continue
        offense = data[column]
        position = _after(data, column)
        for name, lookup in (
            ('offense_category', codes.OFFENSE_CATEGORIES),
            ('crime_against', codes.CRIMES_AGAINST),
            ('offense_group', codes.OFFENSE_GROUPS)):
            data.insert(
                position, f'{prefix}{name}',
                _lookup(offense, lookup.get).astype('category'))
            position += 1
    return data

def decode(
    data: _Table,
    columns: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    codebooks: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, str]] | None = None) -> _Table:
    """Replaces codes with their labels.

    Args:
        data: a table with columns of codes, or an `amos.Dataset` of one
            (whose data is decoded in place).
        columns: the columns to decode. Defaults to `None`, which decodes
            every column of codes in `CODE_COLUMNS` (except age codes, which
            `add_ages` turns into years).
        codebooks: codebooks to use instead of those in
            `crimepy.nibrs.codes.CODEBOOKS`, by column. Defaults to `None`.

    Returns:
        The table (or dataset), with labels (as categories) instead of codes.
            Codes that are not in a codebook are kept.

    """
    if isinstance(data, amos.Dataset):
        data.replace(decode(data.data, columns, codebooks))
        return data
    codebooks = codebooks or {}
    if columns is None:
        columns = [
            c for c in data.columns
            if c in CODE_COLUMNS and CODE_COLUMNS[c] not in _KEPT_CODEBOOKS]
    for column in columns:
        book = codebooks.get(column) or codes.CODEBOOKS[CODE_COLUMNS[column]]
        data[column] = _relabel(data[column], book)
    return data

    if 'state_code' in data.columns and 'state' not in data.columns:
        state = _lookup(data['state_code'], codes.STATE_ABBREVIATIONS.get)
        data.insert(

            state.astype('category'))
    data = add_ages(data)
    data = add_offense_details(data)
    if table == 'agencies':
        data = _add_agency_totals(data)
    return _decode(data) if decode else data

docs.text:
Reads and parses NIBRS master files.

A master file is read one record at a time from its zip archive, without extracting it (recent files are over 6 GB of text). The records are sorted into tables by their segment level and parsed in chunks: each chunk of a segment becomes a grid of characters, and every field is sliced from the grid at once, so even the largest files are parsed in a few minutes.

Each table has a column for each field of its layout (see crimepy.nibrs.layouts), and two more:

  • data_year: the year of the master file.
  • agency_ori: the ORI of the batch header that the record follows. The records of an agency follow its batch header, and their ORIs usually match it, but the FBI notes that the last two characters may differ.

Pre-2013 files split each batch header into three records ("B1", "B2", and "B3"), which are joined into one row of the "agencies" table, so that it has the same columns in every year.

Contents

open_master: opens the text of a master file for reading. parse: parses records of one segment level into a table. read: reads tables from a master file into amos datasets. records: yields the records of a master file. tables: yields the tables of a master file in chunks. year_of: finds the year of a master file from its name.

@contextlib.contextmanager
def open_master(path: pathlib.Path | str) -> Iterator[IO[bytes]]:
    """Opens the text of a master file for reading, as bytes.

    Args:
        path: path of a master file: a zip archive (as the CDE publishes it,
            compressed with Deflate or Deflate64) or the text file in it.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: if there is no file at `path`.
        ValueError: if a zip archive is empty.

    Yields:
        IO[bytes]: the text of the master file.

    """
    path = pathlib.Path(path)
    if not path.is_file():
        message = f'there is no master file at {path}'
        raise FileNotFoundError(message)
    if not zipfile.is_zipfile(path):
        with open(path, 'rb') as stream:
            yield stream
        return
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as archive:
        members = [i for i in archive.infolist() if not i.is_dir()]
        if not members:
            message = f'the zip archive at {path} is empty'
            raise ValueError(message)
        info = max(members, key = lambda i: i.file_size)
        if info.compress_type == _DEFLATE64:
            raw = _Deflate64(path, info)
            with io.BufferedReader(raw, buffer_size = _BLOCK) as stream:
                yield stream
        else:
            with archive.open(info) as stream:
                yield stream

def parse(
    lines: Sequence[bytes],
    layout: layouts.Layout | str,
    **constants: Any) -> pa.Table:
    """Parses records of one segment level into a table.

    Args:
        lines: the records, as bytes, all of the level of `layout`.
        layout: the layout of the records, or its segment level (such as
            "04").
        **constants: columns to add before the fields, each with one value
            for every record (such as `data_year = 2023`), or a sequence of
            values, one for each record.

    Returns:
        A table with a column for each constant and each field.

    """
    if isinstance(layout, str):
        layout = layouts.LAYOUTS[layout]
    columns: dict[str, pa.Array] = {}
    size = len(lines)
    for name, value in constants.items():
        columns[name] = _constant(value, size)
    if size == 0:
        for field in layout:
            columns[field.name] = pa.array([], type = _TYPES[field.kind])
        return pa.table(columns)
    width = layout.width
    text = b''.join(line[:width].ljust(width) for line in lines)
    grid = np.frombuffer(text, dtype = np.uint8).reshape(size, width)
    for field in layout:
        cells = np.ascontiguousarray(grid[:, field.start:field.end])
        columns[field.name] = _convert(
            cells.view(f'S{field.width}').ravel(), field)
    return pa.table(columns)

def read(
    path: pathlib.Path | str,
    names: Sequence[str] | str | None = None,
    *,
    year: int | None = None,
    states: Sequence[str] | str | None = None,
    decode: bool = True,
    chunk_size: int | None = None,
    limit: int | None = None) -> dict[str, amos.Dataset]:
    """Reads tables from a master file into `amos` datasets.

    Everything is kept in memory, so reading a whole recent year (tens of
    millions of records) needs a lot of it. To work with whole years, convert
    them to parquet files once with `crimepy.nibrs.convert` and load what you
    need with `crimepy.nibrs.load`. `read` suits a few states, a few tables,
    or a quick look (with `limit`).

    Args:
        path: path of a master file (see `open_master`).
        names: the tables to read (see `crimepy.nibrs.layouts.TABLES`).
            Defaults to `None`, which reads them all.
        year: the year of the master file. Defaults to `None`, in which case
            it is found from the file's name.
        states: postal abbreviations or numeric state codes of the states to
            keep. Defaults to `None`, which keeps every state.
        decode: whether to replace codes with their labels (see
            `crimepy.nibrs.munge.prepare`). Defaults to `True`.
        chunk_size: the number of records to parse at once. Defaults to
            `None`, in which case it is `crimepy.options.CHUNK_SIZE`.
        limit: the number of records to read before stopping. Defaults to
            `None`, which reads them all.

    Returns:
        A dataset for each table, by name, whose `data` is the table.

    """
    wanted = _wanted(names)
    parts: dict[str, list[pa.Table]] = {name: [] for name in wanted}
    for chunk in tables(
        path, wanted, year = year, states = states, chunk_size = chunk_size,
        limit = limit):
        for name, table in chunk.items():
            parts[name].append(table)
    datasets = {}
    for name, pieces in parts.items():
        table = (
            pa.concat_tables(pieces) if pieces
            else schema(name).empty_table())
        frame = munge.prepare(munge.to_pandas(table), name, decode = decode)
        datasets[name] = amos.Dataset.create(frame)
    return datasets

    """Returns the columns and types of a table of a master file.

            f'{sorted(layouts.SEGMENTS)}')

def tables(
    path: pathlib.Path | str,
    names: Sequence[str] | str | None = None,
    *,
    year: int | None = None,
    states: Sequence[str] | str | None = None,
    chunk_size: int | None = None,
    limit: int | None = None,
    progress: Callable[[int], None] | None = None) -> Iterator[_Chunk]:
    """Yields the tables of a master file, a chunk of records at a time.

    Args:
        path: path of a master file (see `open_master`).
        names: the tables to make (see `crimepy.nibrs.layouts.TABLES`).
            Defaults to `None`, which makes them all.
        year: the year of the master file. Defaults to `None`, in which case
            it is found from the file's name (see `year_of`).
        states: postal abbreviations (such as "DE") or numeric state codes
            (such as "07") of the states to keep. Defaults to `None`, which
            keeps every state.
        chunk_size: the number of records to parse at once. Defaults to
            `None`, in which case it is `crimepy.options.CHUNK_SIZE`.
        limit: the number of records to read before stopping. Defaults to
            `None`, which reads them all.
        progress: called with the number of records read so far after each
            chunk. Defaults to `None`.

    Yields:
        dict[str, pa.Table]: for each chunk, the tables that have records in
            it, by name. The "agencies" table, which is small, comes in the
            last chunk.

    """
    wanted = _wanted(names)
    levels = {
        level.encode() for name in wanted
        for level in layouts.SEGMENTS[name]}
    kept = _state_codes(states)
    year = year if year is not None else year_of(path)
    chunk_size = chunk_size or options.CHUNK_SIZE
    batch: dict[bytes, list[bytes]] = collections.defaultdict(list)
    owners: dict[bytes, list[bytes]] = collections.defaultdict(list)
    headers: dict[str, list[bytes]] = collections.defaultdict(list)
    owner = b''
    count = 0
    pending = 0
    for record in records(path):
        if limit is not None and count >= limit:
            break
        count += 1
        level = record[:2]
        if level in _HEADERS:
            owner = record[4:13]
        if level not in levels or (kept and record[2:4] not in kept):
            continue
        if level[0:1] == b'B':
            headers[level.decode()].append(record)
            continue
        batch[level].append(record)
        owners[level].append(owner)
        pending += 1
        if pending >= chunk_size:
            yield _parse_batch(batch, owners, year)
            batch.clear()
            owners.clear()
            pending = 0
            if progress is not None:
                progress(count)
    parsed = _parse_batch(batch, owners, year)
    if 'agencies' in wanted:
        parsed['agencies'] = _agencies(headers, year)
    if progress is not None:
        progress(count)
    yield parsed

def year_of(path: pathlib.Path | str) -> int | None:
    """Returns the year of a master file, found from its name.

    Args:
        path: path of a master file, such as "nibrs-2023.zip".

    Returns:
        The year, or `None` if the name does not have one.

    """
    path = pathlib.Path(path)
    found = _YEAR.search(path.name)
    if found:
        return int(found.group(1))
    names = [path.name]
    if zipfile.is_zipfile(path):
        with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as archive:
            names.extend(archive.namelist())
    for name in names:
        found = _YEAR.search(name)
        if found:
            return int(found.group(1))
        short = _SHORT_YEAR.search(name)
        if short:
            year = int(short.group(1))
            return year + (1900 if year >= 90 else 2000)
    return None

A master file is read and parsed once by convert, which saves each table of the year as a parquet file in the "nibrs/tables/{year}" folder of the data folder. load then reads any table of any years from those files, keeping only the states and columns asked for, which takes seconds instead of the minutes that parsing a master file takes. load downloads and converts the years that are missing, so it is usually the only function needed. def convert(
    years: Any,
    folder: pathlib.Path | str | None = None,
    *,
    tables: Sequence[str] | str | None = None,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    progress: bool = True,
    chunk_size: int | None = None) -> dict[int, dict[str, pathlib.Path]]:
    """Converts the NIBRS master files of years to parquet files.

    Master files that have not been downloaded are downloaded first. Tables
    that were converted before are skipped unless `overwrite` is true, and a
    year whose tables were all converted before is not read again.

    Args:
        years: a year, years, or a range of years (see
            `crimepy.utilities.to_years`).
        folder: the data folder. Defaults to `None`, in which case it is
            `crimepy.utilities.data_folder()`.
        tables: the tables to convert. Defaults to `None`, which converts
            them all.
        overwrite: whether to convert tables that were converted before (and
            to download their master files again). Defaults to `False`.
        progress: whether to show progress. Defaults to `True`.
        chunk_size: the number of records to parse at once. Defaults to
            `None`, in which case it is `crimepy.options.CHUNK_SIZE`.

    Returns:
        For each year, the path of each table's parquet file.

    """
    names = reader._wanted(tables)
    converted = {}
    for year in utilities.to_years(years):
        paths = {n: table_path(n, year, folder) for n in names}
        missing = [n for n, p in paths.items() if overwrite or not p.is_file()]
        if missing:
            master = cde.master_path(year, folder)
            if overwrite or not master.is_file():
                cde.download(
                    year, folder, overwrite = overwrite, progress = progress)
            _write(master, year, missing, paths, progress, chunk_size)
        converted[year] = paths
    return converted

def load_frame(
    table: str,
    years: Any,
    *,
    folder: pathlib.Path | str | None = None,
    states: Sequence[str] | str | None = None,
    columns: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    decode: bool = True,
    fetch: bool = True,
    progress: bool = True) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Loads a table of NIBRS data for years into a `pandas` data frame.

    The years are stacked into one table, with "data_year" saying which
    master file each row came from. `load` returns the same table as an
    `amos.Dataset`.

    Args:
        table: the name of the table: "administrative", "offenses",
            "properties", "victims", "offenders", "arrestees",
            "group_b_arrests", "window_clearances", "window_properties",
            "window_arrestees", or "agencies".
        years: a year, years, or a range of years (see
            `crimepy.utilities.to_years`).
        folder: the data folder. Defaults to `None`, in which case it is
            `crimepy.utilities.data_folder()`.
        states: postal abbreviations (such as "DE") or numeric state codes
            of the states to keep. Defaults to `None`, which keeps every
            state.
        columns: the columns to load. Defaults to `None`, which loads them
            all. Columns that `crimepy.nibrs.munge.prepare` adds (such as
            "state") are added if the columns they come from are loaded.
        decode: whether to replace codes with their labels. Defaults to
            `True`.
        fetch: whether to download and convert years that have not been
            converted. Defaults to `True`.
        progress: whether to show the progress of downloads and conversions.
            Defaults to `True`.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: if a year has not been converted and `fetch` is
            false.

    Returns:
        The table.

    """
    schema = reader.schema(table)
    paths = []
    for year in utilities.to_years(years):
        path = table_path(table, year, folder)
        if not path.is_file():
            if not fetch:
                message = (
                    f'the {table} of {year} have not been converted: use '
                    f'crimepy.nibrs.convert({year}) or fetch = True')
                raise FileNotFoundError(message)
            convert(year, folder, progress = progress)
        paths.append(path)
    if not paths:
        message = 'there are no years to load'
        raise ValueError(message)
    if columns is not None:
        unknown = [c for c in columns if c not in schema.names]
        if unknown:
            message = f'{table!r} has no columns {unknown}'
            raise KeyError(message)
    dataset = ds.dataset(
        [str(p) for p in paths], schema = schema, format = 'parquet')
    kept = reader._state_codes(states)
    condition = (
        ds.field('state_code').isin([c.decode() for c in kept])
        if kept else None)
    loaded = dataset.to_table(
        columns = list(columns) if columns is not None else None,
        filter = condition)
    return munge.prepare(munge.to_pandas(loaded), table, decode = decode)

docs.text:
Joins the tables of NIBRS incidents into flat tables for analysis.

The master files spread each incident over several tables (its offenses, victims, offenders, and arrestees), and an analysis usually needs them together. Each builder here returns one flat table with one row for each incident, victim, offense, offender, or arrestee, and the details of its incident and agency:

  • incidents: one row for each incident, with its agency; the number of its offenses, victims, offenders, and arrestees; whether it had an offense against a person, property, or society, and an offense of each category; whether a firearm was used; whether and when someone was arrested; and whether it was cleared.
  • victims: one row for each victim, with its incident and agency, and the age, sex, race, and ethnicity of the first offender that the victim is related to, with the relationship.
  • offenses: one row for each offense, with its incident and agency.
  • offenders: one row for each offender, with its incident and agency.
  • arrestees: one row for each arrestee, with its incident and agency.

build loads what a builder needs and calls it. Each builder takes the segments as amos datasets or data frames and returns an amos.Dataset, whose data is the built table (and which can be given a label, task, and groups for modeling):

import crimepy

victims = crimepy.nibrs.tables.build('victims', 2022, states = 'DE')
victims.data.head()

The tables of an incident share the columns in KEYS. Agencies are joined by the ORI of the batch header that each record follows ("agency_ori"), and their columns get the prefix "agency_" (such as "agency_population").

Contents

AGENCY_COLUMNS: the columns of agencies that are joined to incidents. BUILDERS: the builders, by name. KEYS: the columns that identify an incident. arrestees: one row for each arrestee. build: loads the tables that a builder needs and builds its table. incidents: one row for each incident. offenders: one row for each offender. offenses: one row for each offense. victims: one row for each victim.

@_dataset_builder
def incidents(
    segments: Mapping[str, pd.DataFrame],
    *,
    categories: bool = True) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns one row for each incident.

    Args:
        segments: the tables of the incidents (as datasets or data
            frames), by name. "administrative" is
            needed. "offenses", "victims", "offenders", "arrestees", and
            "agencies" are used if they are there.
        categories: whether to add a column for each category of offense
            (such as "has_assault_offenses"), saying whether the incident had
            an offense of that category. Defaults to `True`.

    Raises:
        KeyError: if there is no "administrative" table.

    Returns:
        The incidents (once each, though a few are in the master files more
            than once), with the columns of the administrative segment and:
            "incident_weekday" and "incident_month"; the agency's columns
            (see `AGENCY_COLUMNS`); "offense_count", "victim_count",
            "offender_count" (offenders whose sequence number is not 0,
            which means unknown), and "arrestee_count"; "against_person",
            "against_property", and "against_society"; "firearm";
            "arrested", "first_arrest_date", and "days_to_arrest"; and
            "cleared" (by an arrest or exceptionally).

    """
    # A few incidents are in the master files more than once (193 of the 12
    # million in 2023), so only the first record of each is kept.
    data = _require(segments, 'administrative').drop_duplicates(KEYS)
    dates = pd.to_datetime(data['incident_date'])
    data['incident_weekday'] = pd.Categorical(
        dates.dt.day_name(),
        categories = [
            'Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday',
            'Saturday', 'Sunday'])
    data['incident_month'] = dates.dt.month.astype('Int64')
    data = _join_agencies(data, segments.get('agencies'))
    offense_table = segments.get('offenses')
    if offense_table is not None:
        data = _join_offense_summary(data, offense_table, categories)
    counted = (('victims', 'victim_count'), ('offenders', 'offender_count'))
    for name, column in counted:
        table = segments.get(name)
        if table is not None:
            if name == 'offenders':
                table = table[table['offender_sequence'].fillna(0) > 0]
            data = _join_counts(data, table, column)
    arrests = segments.get('arrestees')
    if arrests is not None:
        data = _join_counts(data, arrests, 'arrestee_count')
        first = arrests.groupby(KEYS, observed = True)['arrest_date'].min()
        data = data.merge(
            first.rename('first_arrest_date').reset_index(), on = KEYS,
            how = 'left')
        data['arrested'] = data['arrestee_count'] > 0
        data['days_to_arrest'] = (
            data['first_arrest_date'] - pd.to_datetime(data['incident_date'])
        ).dt.days.astype('Int64')
    exceptional = data['cleared_exceptionally'].astype('object')
    cleared = exceptional.notna() & ~exceptional.isin(_NOT_CLEARED)
    if 'arrested' in data.columns:
        cleared = cleared | data['arrested']
    data['cleared'] = cleared.astype('boolean')
    return data

def victims(segments: Mapping[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns one row for each victim.

    Args:
        segments: the tables of the incidents (as datasets or data
            frames), by name. "victims" is needed.

    Returns:

            the agency's columns, and, from the first offender that the
            victim is related to: "offender_sequence", "relationship",
            "offender_age", "offender_sex", "offender_race", and
            "offender_ethnicity".

    """
    data = _with_incident(_require(segments, 'victims'), segments)
    offenders_ = segments.get('offenders')
    if offenders_ is not None:
        data['offender_sequence'] = data['offender_1'].astype('Int64')
        data['relationship'] = data['relationship_1']
        columns = [
            c for c in (
                'offender_age', 'offender_sex', 'offender_race',
                'offender_ethnicity')
            if c in offenders_.columns]
        people = offenders_[[*KEYS, 'offender_sequence', *columns]]
        people = people.drop_duplicates([*KEYS, 'offender_sequence'])
        people = people.astype({'offender_sequence': 'Int64'})
        data = data.merge(
            people, on = [*KEYS, 'offender_sequence'], how = 'left')
    return data

def apply(self, item: amos.Dataset, **kwargs: Any) -> amos.Dataset:
    """Loads the table, as a dataset that continues `item`.

    Args:
        item: the dataset so far, whose seed and history are kept.
        **kwargs: the parameters (see the class's documentation).

    Returns:
        The dataset of the table.

    """
    kwargs.pop('source', None)
    label = kwargs.pop('label', None) or item.label
    task = kwargs.pop('task', None)
    groups = utilities.to_names(kwargs.pop('groups', None) or item.groups)
    data = self.load('nibrs', **kwargs)
    if label not in data.columns:
        label, task = None, None
    groups = [g for g in groups if g in data.columns]
    loaded = amos.Dataset.create(
        data, label = label, task = task, seed = item.seed,
        groups = groups or None, use_gpu = item.use_gpu)
    loaded.history = item.history
    loaded.record(
        self.name, source = 'nibrs', rows = len(data),
        columns = len(data.columns))
    return loaded

        states: the states to keep. Defaults to `None`, which keeps every
            state.
        columns: the columns to keep. Defaults to `None`, which keeps
            them all.
        decode: whether to replace codes with their labels. Defaults to
            `True`.
        folder: the data folder. Defaults to `None`, in which case it is
            `crimepy.utilities.data_folder()`.
        **kwargs: arguments for the builder of a built table.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if no years are given.

    Returns:
        The table.

    """
    if not utilities.to_years(years):
        message = (
            f'set the "years" of {self.name!r} in the '
            f'"{self.name}_parameters" section of the settings')
        raise ValueError(message)
    wanted = utilities.to_names(columns) or None
    decode = utilities.to_bool(decode)
    if table in tables.BUILDERS:
        data = tables.build(
            table, years, states = states, folder = folder,
            decode = decode, **kwargs).data
        return data[wanted] if wanted else data
    return store.load_frame(
        table, years, states = states, columns = wanted, decode = decode,
        folder = folder)
